rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Gravitational redshift of gamma rays over a 22.5 m tower; (5.13 +/- 0.51)e-15 vs 4.92e-15 predicted.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Predicted relativistic time gains for caesium clocks flown around the world (-40 +/- 23 ns east, 275 +/- 21 ns west).

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Observed relativistic time gains (-59 +/- 10 ns east, 273 +/- 7 ns west).

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.collaboration: Gravity Probe A (SAO / NASA, Vessot et al.)
rows.note: Space-borne hydrogen maser to ~10,000 km; gravitational frequency shift agrees with prediction to ~70 ppm.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Two Al+ optical clocks, 33 cm height difference; (4.1 +/- 1.6)e-17 measured vs 3.6e-17 predicted.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: Gravitational redshift resolved across one millimetre within a single strontium atom cloud; one collaboration at that scale.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Prediction of the gravitational redshift and the clock-rate dependence on potential; the derivation parent for T.01's DERIVED claims.

rows.label: OPEN
rows.note: Standard survey of experimental tests of general relativity; anchors the OPEN statement that the measurements do not pick between the two descriptions.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Special relativity: the Lorentz factor and time dilation; derivation parent for the four-velocity statement.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Transverse Doppler shift of canal rays: first laboratory measurement of time dilation.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.collaboration: Botermann et al. (GSI ESR storage ring)
rows.note: Li+ ions at about a third of c: Lorentz time dilation confirmed at high precision.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Relativity in the Global Positioning System: the derivation of the ~38 us/day net satellite clock offset.

rows.label: BOUND
rows.note: GRB 221009A: Lorentz-invariance violation bounds E_QG,1 > 10 E_Pl and E_QG,2 > 6e-8 E_Pl at 95% CL.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: The foundation of general relativity: field equation whose weak-field static limit is Poisson's equation.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Final result: eta(Ti,Pt) = (-1.5 +/- 2.3 stat +/- 1.5 syst) x 1e-15.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Torsion-balance test of the equivalence principle: eta(Be,Ti) = (0.3 +/- 1.8) x 1e-13.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Lunar laser ranging test of the equivalence principle for Earth and Moon falling toward the Sun.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: Antihydrogen falls down: a = (0.75 +/- 0.13 +/- 0.16) g; one collaboration, no independent replication.

rows.label: OPEN
rows.note: Survey of equivalence-principle and metric tests; anchors the OPEN statement about what fixes G and why universality holds.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Molecular-beam magnetic resonance: a two-level system driven at its Bohr frequency; the measured face of Schroedinger evolution.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Separated oscillatory fields: phase accumulated by a two-level system between two interaction zones, the method behind atomic clocks.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Spin echoes: free precession of spins refocused by a pulse; unitary two-level evolution measured in time.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Canonical quantum gravity: the Hamiltonian constraint H Psi = 0, the equation with no time in it.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Evolution without evolution: conditioning a stationary global state on a clock subsystem recovers Schroedinger evolution.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: Photonic illustration of Page-Wootters time from entanglement; the only realisation to date.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Quantum reference frames: covariance of physical laws under changes of quantum frame; which clock is a frame-dependent question.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Preprint arguing a 'preferred-time problem' remains in Page-Wootters constructions; PROPOSED at most until peer review.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Interferometric visibility of a clock in superposition of heights: V = |cos(Delta E Delta tau / 2 hbar)|; a proposal, derived.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: A self-interfering clock as a which-path witness: visibility loss from a clock-rate difference made by a magnetic gradient, not gravity.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Superposition of proper times in trapped-atom interferometers: predicted visibility modulation and resonance shift; not realised.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Quantum signatures of proper time in optical ion clocks ('proper time interferometry'); a proposal, not a measurement.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Universal master equation for gravity-related decoherence; the model this page tests, labelled as a proposal.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Gravity's role in quantum state reduction: collapse time tau ~ hbar / E_G from the gravitational self-energy of the difference between the two mass distributions.

rows.label: BOUND
rows.collaboration: Donadi, Piscicchia, Curceanu, Diosi, Laubenstein & Bassi (LNGS Gran Sasso)
rows.note: Underground germanium detector: no spontaneous-radiation excess; lower bound on R0 about three orders of magnitude above previous bounds; parameter-free Diosi-Penrose ruled out.

rows.label: BOUND
rows.note: Electronic recoils 1-140 keV, first science run: Diosi-Penrose limits improved by a factor of five, CSL by two orders of magnitude (CSL is out of this page's scope). Young row: supports SINGLE RESULT at most.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: Quantum superposition of molecules beyond 25 kDa: the heaviest matter-wave interference to date; the scale where DP predictions start to bite.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Gravitational radiation from colliding black holes: the area theorem, the horizon area never decreases.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Black holes and entropy: entropy proportional to horizon area.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Particle creation by black holes: thermal radiation and the information question.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Average entropy of a subsystem: S(m,n) = sum_{k=n+1}^{mn} 1/k - (m-1)/(2n); the closed form the toy is checked against.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.collaboration: Page (Physical Review Letters, information in radiation)
rows.note: Information in black hole radiation: the Page curve, radiation entropy rises then falls if evaporation is unitary.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: GW150914: first observation of gravitational waves from a binary black hole merger.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.collaboration: Isi, Farr, Giesler, Scheel & Teukolsky (Caltech / Flatiron)
rows.note: Testing the black-hole area law with GW150914: an independent analysis of the public data; the first area-theorem test.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: GW250114: network SNR 80; remnant area larger than the sum of the initial areas to high credibility; mode frequencies within 30 percent of Kerr. Young row.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Entanglement wedge reconstruction and the information paradox: quantum extremal surfaces give a Page curve.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: The entropy of bulk quantum fields and the entanglement wedge of an evaporating black hole.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: An apologia for islands: defends the island mechanism; preprint, PROPOSED at most.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.collaboration: Geng, Karch, Perez-Pardavila, Raju, Randall & Riojas (arXiv preprint)
rows.note: Seeing Page curves and islands with blinders on: argues islands only redistribute information when a detector has a blind spot; preprint, PROPOSED at most.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.collaboration: Bose, Mazumdar, Morley, Ulbricht, Toros, Paternostro, Geraci, Barker, Kim & Milburn (PRL)
rows.note: Spin entanglement witness for quantum gravity: two micron-size masses in adjacent interferometers; illustrative geometry 1e-14 kg, 450 um apart, split by 250 um, 2.5 s; witness W > 1 certifies entanglement. A proposal, not performed.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Gravitationally induced entanglement between two masses is argued to be sufficient evidence of quantum effects in gravity, via a general information-theoretic argument about mediators. A proposal.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Gravitational coupling between two gold spheres of about 1 mm radius and 90 mg, torsion pendulum, 12.7 mHz, 350 h; closest surface distance 400 um. Newtonian gravity measured from a source below 100 mg.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.collaboration: Fuchs, Uitenbroek, Plugge, van Halteren, van Soest, Vinante, Ulbricht & Oosterkamp (Leiden)
rows.note: Levitated 0.4 mg magnetic particle at 26.7 Hz, Q above 1e7, force noise 0.5 fN/sqrt(Hz), senses kilogram source masses about half a metre away. Gravity sensed by a sub-milligram test mass.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: One-milligram torsional pendulum at 18 Hz laser-cooled from room temperature to 240 microkelvin; a platform, not a gravity or entanglement measurement. Young row.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.collaboration: Troyer, Fechtel, Hummer, Rudolph, Stickler, Delic & Arndt (Vienna)
rows.note: Two librational modes of a levitated silica nanorotor cooled to occupation numbers 0.21 +/- 0.03 and 0.54 +/- 0.32 singly, 1.02 +/- 0.08 and 0.73 +/- 0.22 together. Young row.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: A classical channel model for gravitational decoherence: gravity as measurement and feedback (LOCC) reproduces the Newtonian force but entangles nothing and adds a minimum decoherence. The LOCC channel of this page.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Separability criterion: a separable density matrix has a positive partial transpose; for two qubits the criterion is necessary and sufficient. The negativity readout of this page.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Concurrence of an arbitrary two-qubit state; for a pure state C = 2|ad - bc|, which for the four-branch gravitational state is |sin(delta phi / 2)|.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Argues that the classical gravitational interaction can transmit quantum information and generate entanglement through physically local processes when matter is treated by quantum field theory. Disputed; young row.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Diosi-Penrose dynamics with classical gravity can entangle the mechanical degrees of freedom of two separate particles; 'GIE detection is not enough to validate quantum gravity'. Young row.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: A demonstration that classical gravity does not produce entanglement: if gravity is classical and a mediator and entanglement is observed, something other than gravity supplied it. Young row.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Two-page rebuttal: classical gravity cannot mediate entanglement by local means; quantum features are necessary in the field if it entangles by local propagation. Preprint, PROPOSED at most.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Non-perturbative Heisenberg-picture derivation said to preclude the entanglement claimed by Aziz and Howl. Preprint, PROPOSED at most.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Proposal to test whether gravity can entangle a levitated particle with an array of quantum clocks; the quantised active gravitational mass has not been tested in any prior experiment. Preprint.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Sourcing semiclassical gravity from spontaneously localized quantum matter: the hybrid classical-gravity / quantum-matter construction whose master equation (Newtonian pair potential plus doubled DP decoherence, sigma smearing) Trillo and Navascues integrate. A proposal.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.collaboration: Van De Kamp, Marshman, Bose & Mazumdar (PRA)
rows.note: Quantum gravity witness via entanglement of masses with Casimir screening: the geometry (1e-15 kg, 23 um split, 24 um separation) that Trillo and Navascues take for their Fig. 3. A proposal.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.collaboration: Lee, Adelberger, Cook, Fleischer & Heckel (Eot-Wash, University of Washington)
rows.note: New test of the gravitational 1/r^2 law at separations down to 52 um: data between 52 um and 3.0 mm; any gravitational-strength Yukawa interaction limited to ranges below 38.6 um at 95 % confidence. Wedge geometry on the page from J. G. Lee's 2020 dissertation (University of Washington, hdl.handle.net/1773/45542, Tables 4.1-4.5, 4.8).

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.collaboration: Tan et al. (HUST, Huazhong University of Science and Technology)
rows.note: Improvement for testing the gravitational inverse-square law at the submillimeter range: |alpha| <= 1 holds down to lambda = 48 um at 95 % confidence; strongest bound on alpha in the range 40-350 um. Apparatus geometry (from the 2026 review by Murata, Fujiie & Suzuki, Fig. 8): two 0.2 mm tungsten pendulum plates facing a 1.8 mm tungsten plate at a 210 um surface gap, a rotating eight-plate far source, a 30 um Be-Cu shield; the modulation and compensation scheme is not in open text.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.collaboration: Lee, Adelberger, Marcoline, Terrano & Heckel (Eot-Wash, University of Washington)
rows.note: The Fourier-Bessel expansion applied to experimental probes of gravity and feeble short-range interactions: the torque between two N-fold wedge-patterned plates as one integral over wavenumber (their Eqs. 7-19); the formalism this page's wedge kernel rebuilds.

rows.label: BOUND
rows.collaboration: Helou, Slagmolen, McClelland & Chen (LISA Pathfinder data)
rows.note: LISA Pathfinder appreciably constrains collapse models: the Diosi-Penrose regularisation scale sigma_DP bounded from below at 40.1 +/- 0.5 fm, larger than any nucleus.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Orch-OR review: consciousness-related collapse follows 'the specific Diosi-Penrose (DP) scheme of objective reduction'; the one biological use of the DP parameter on the ladder. A proposal; the page does not assess it.

rows.label: BOUND
rows.note: Gravitationally induced decoherence vs space-time diffusion: a decoherence-diffusion trade-off for any consistent classical-gravity / quantum-matter theory; torsion-balance data bound the diffusion, D2 <= 1e-41 kg^2 s m^-3; the Diosi-Penrose kernel named as a member of the class.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Diffusion minimization via optimal smearing in collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models (GRW, CSL, DP, Tilloy-Diosi): notes that for the smearing length 'upper bounds can be put by observing no deviations from Newton's law of gravitation' without working one out. Preprint; young row.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Short-range tests of the gravitational inverse-square law (review): the UW 2020 geometry in its Fig. 7 caption and the HUST 2020 geometry in its Fig. 8 caption; no smeared or erf-type potential anywhere in it; preprint, young row, cited for geometry only.
